slides.head:
Critics say David Fincher's new film
uses generative AI. It's unconfirmed.
A sequel with big names.
slides.body: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is directed by David Fincher from a Quentin Tarantino script, with Brad Pitt back as Cliff Booth. It opens in IMAX November 25 and on Netflix December 23.

slides.head: The first complaints.
slides.body: On November 19, indie filmmaker Patrick Tomasso posted that the film has "blatant and egregious AI use." A Next Best Picture review called it "nothing but an eyesore."

slides.head: A credit raised questions.
slides.body: Entertainment writer Louis Peitzman noted a "generative supervisor" listed in the credits. Neither review said which scenes may have used AI.

slides.head: Fincher has not confirmed it.
slides.body: Asked about the technology by the LA Times, he said: "Well, it exists. Should we not use it?" Netflix did not immediately respond to TheWrap's request for comment.

slides.head: Say how you made it.
slides.body: This argument started with a credit and a few frames, not a statement. If you use AI in your work, say where, before someone else says it for you.
